publicSlug.description: The venue's public web address, `/venues/{publicSlug}` (#355). Unique across EVERY club, unlike `slug`; filled by a database trigger when a venue is created and never changed after (P41), so a shared link keeps working. Null only for a venue the backfill missed, which should be none; the web lists such a venue without linking it. Native clients keep addressing venues by `id`.

sports.description: Distinct sports over the ACTIVE resources listed below (capped at 50 here).

fromPriceCents.description: Lowest `basePriceCents` among ACTIVE resources, integer CENTS; null when there are none.

coverPhotoUrl.description: The cover's default URL (`cover.url`), kept for clients that predate `cover`. Prefer `cover`, which carries every width and the alt text.

cover.description: The venue's cover photo (#366), or null when the club has not uploaded one.

description.description: Plaintext. The schema comment claims "encrypted at rest"; nothing encrypts or decrypts this column today, so it is returned as stored.

lat.description: WGS-84. Decimal(10,7) in the database, coerced to a JSON number at the DTO boundary — it is a number on the wire, not a string.

lng.description: WGS-84, coerced to a JSON number. See `lat`.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. "Europe/Sofia". This is the zone `?date=` on the availability endpoint is resolved in.

openingHours.description: The venue's `openingHoursJson` column, passed through verbatim. No shape is enforced anywhere in the codebase and nothing else reads it; the column default is `{}`. Modelled as free-form JSON on purpose — do not generate a typed struct for it.

photos.description: The venue's gallery (#366), in the order the club set; at most 12. The cover is `cover`, never repeated here. Empty when there are none.

VenueSummaryPage.description: The `data` of a paged venue response (`page()` in _lib/envelope.ts).

nextCursor.description: Opaque; pass back verbatim as `?cursor=`. Null on the last page. (It is currently the last item's venue id — keyset pagination on `id asc` — but clients must not parse it.)

NearVenue.description: A venue from the geo search. NOT a `VenueSummary`: it adds `distanceKm` and omits `sports`, `fromPriceCents` and `coverPhotoUrl`. A client that needs those must fetch `GET /venues/{id}`.

distanceKm.description: Great-circle distance from the query point, computed with PostGIS `geography` and rounded to one decimal place.

NearVenueResult.description: The `data` of `GET /venues/near`. The echoed `radiusKm` and `maxResults` are part of the contract: a caller that asked for 500 km and got 50 must be able to tell, rather than rendering "nothing within 500 km".

radiusKm.description: The radius ACTUALLY used after clamping, not the one requested. Max 50, default 10.

paginated.description: Always false. This endpoint has no page two by design — a distance-ordered cursor is unstable once the caller moves. Widen `radiusKm` instead.

AvailabilitySlot.description: One candidate booking window. Half-open [startTs, endTs); its length is the resource's `minBookingMinutes`, and consecutive slots are `slotStepMinutes` apart, so slots OVERLAP whenever the step is smaller than the minimum booking.

priceCents.description: Integer CENTS for this slot after pricing rules are applied, in the parent resource's `currency`.

available.description: False when a PENDING or CONFIRMED booking overlaps. Unavailable slots are returned deliberately, so the client can grey them out rather than making the club look shut.

blockedReason.description: Present ONLY when `available` is false. Currently always the literal "booked".

durations.description: Present ONLY when `available` is true: every length a booking starting here can have — whole units of `minBookingMinutes` up to `maxBookingMinutes`, the whole span free and inside one opening window — shortest first. The first entry is the slot itself. A snapshot like the slot: the booking's INSERT still decides (409 `SLOT_TAKEN`).

ResourceSlots.description: One ACTIVE resource and its materialised slots for the requested window.

currency.description: ISO 4217, e.g. "EUR". The unit for every `priceCents` under this resource.

maxBookingMinutes.description: The longest booking this resource takes, in minutes. `durations` never exceeds it.

slots.description: May be empty when the resource is closed for the whole window. Ordered by day, then by start time within each opening window.

timezone.description: IANA zone of the venue. The client needs it to render "09:00" instead of doing UTC arithmetic — and it is the zone `?date=` was resolved in.

from.description: Start of the window the server actually resolved, RFC 3339 UTC with no fractional seconds. Echoed because the resolution depends on the venue's timezone and on defaults the client did not send.

to.description: Exclusive end of the resolved window, RFC 3339 UTC with no fractional seconds.

resources.description: ACTIVE resources of the venue (capped at 50), ordered by name; narrowed to one when `?resourceId=` is given. EMPTY when the venue has no active resource, or when `resourceId` matches none — that is a 200, not a 404.

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: The v1 booking wire shape, produced by `toBooking` in `src/app/api/v1/_lib/dto.ts`. The venue is deliberately FLATTENED out of the resource, so a client never has to know that the venue hangs off the resource in the database schema. Every field listed is always present; nullables are explicit nulls, never omitted keys.

id.description: Booking id. Also the value used as a pagination cursor.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Known values: `PENDING`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED`, `NO_SHOW`. Deliberately typed as an open string rather than a closed enum — a shipped iOS binary decoding a closed enum would fail outright on a status added later, and this codebase cannot hotfix a binary for a week. Treat an unrecognised value as "unknown" rather than failing the decode.

startTs.description: Start instant, RFC 3339 in UTC with NO fractional seconds (e.g. `2026-09-24T09:00:00Z`). Swift's default `.iso8601` strategy REJECTS fractional seconds, which is why the server strips them.

endTs.description: End instant, RFC 3339 UTC with no fractional seconds.

totalCents.description: The full booking price in integer CENTS of `currency`. Never a float, never a string. Computed server-side at creation and written down; it does not change afterwards.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for `totalCents`, e.g. `EUR` (the column default). Upper-case.

expiresAt.description: When a PENDING booking stops holding its slot — 15 minutes after creation. Since #354 a booking is CONFIRMED when made (paid at the club), so this is `null` for every booking at a pilot club; it is set only at a club that takes payment online. A client should count down against it and stop offering payment when it passes.

cancelledAt.description: When the booking was cancelled, or `null` if it was not.

createdAt.description: When the booking was created. RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds.

cancellableUntil.description: The last instant the PLAYER may cancel this booking in the app (#354): the venue's cancellation cutoff (default 24 h, set by the club) before `startTs`, measured in elapsed hours. `null` when the booking is not cancellable at all (CANCELLED, COMPLETED, NO_SHOW). It may already be in the past: then only the club can cancel, and `POST …/cancel` answers 403 `CANCELLATION_CUTOFF_PASSED`. Render it in `venue.timezone`. RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds.

resource.description: The court/pitch/table booked. Trimmed deliberately: no price, no status, no tenant id.

id.description: Resource id — the same value passed as `resourceId` when creating a booking.

resourceType.description: `ResourceType` (P51): COURT, FIELD, TABLE, BOARD_TABLE, LOBBY, ROUTE or TRACK. A TRACK (karting) is called a "писта" / "track", anything else a court. An open string, as `sport` here: show an unknown value as a court.

venue.description: The club/venue, lifted out of the resource so the wire shape survives a schema change that moves the relation.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. `Europe/Sofia`. The client needs it to render `startTs` as local wall-clock time rather than doing UTC arithmetic.

BookingEnvelope.title: BookingEnvelope
BookingEnvelope.description: The success envelope for a single booking. Every v1 success body is an object from the first commit — a bare value has nowhere to grow a cursor or a deprecation notice without breaking binaries already in the field.

items.description: The bookings on this page, newest `startTs` first. May be empty.

nextCursor.description: OPAQUE. Pass back verbatim as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page; never parse it. `null` means this is the last page. (It is currently the last item's `id`, but that is an implementation detail a client must not rely on.)

BookingPageEnvelope.title: BookingPageEnvelope
BookingPageEnvelope.description: The paginated success envelope: `{"data":{"items":[...],"nextCursor":...}}`. Note the DOUBLE nesting — a client generated against the unwrapped page shape cannot decode this at all.

CreateBookingRequest.title: CreateBookingRequest
CreateBookingRequest.description: Which slot to book. It carries NO price: the server prices the span itself from the resource's base price, opening windows and pricing rules, so a client cannot book a €24 court for one cent. Any price-shaped field sent here is silently ignored. Unknown properties are ignored rather than rejected.

resourceId.description: The resource (court, pitch, table) to book. Must be an ACTIVE resource at an ACTIVE venue belonging to `{slug}`; anything else is a 404. A missing, non-string or blank value is a 400 with `details.field = "resourceId"`.

startTs.description: Start instant, RFC 3339 date-time WITH an offset (`2036-07-16T06:00:00Z` or `…T09:00:00+03:00`); anything else is a 400 `BAD_REQUEST` with `details.field = "startTs"`. Must be in the future. Must fall on a WHOLE MINUTE — any seconds or fractional seconds are rejected, so build this from a clock value rather than from `Date.now()` arithmetic. Must land exactly on the resource's step grid measured FROM THE OPENING TIME (a club opening at 09:15 with 30-minute steps offers 09:15 and 09:45, never 09:30), and must not be an ambiguous local wall clock on a DST fall-back day.

endTs.description: End instant, RFC 3339. Must be after `startTs`, a whole number of minutes later, at least `minBookingMinutes`, at most `maxBookingMinutes`, a whole multiple of `minBookingMinutes`, no more than 4 hours in total, and inside the SAME opening window as `startTs` (a span bridging a lunchtime closure is two bookings, not one).

notes.description: Optional free-text note stored on the booking, at most 500 characters after trimming (#354). A longer note, or a value that is not a string or null, is a 400 `BAD_REQUEST` with `details.field = "notes"`.

CancelBookingRequest.title: CancelBookingRequest
CancelBookingRequest.description: Optional cancellation body. The whole body may be omitted.

reason.description: Free-text reason, recorded on the Cancellation receipt and on the booking. A non-string value is ignored (treated as no reason). Not shown to the player anywhere in this response.

CancelQuote.title: CancelQuote
CancelQuote.description: What the cancellation receipt says. The percentage is RESOLVED AND WRITTEN DOWN at cancellation time, not recomputed later — the club may change its policy next month, and this receipt must not change with it. No money is moved by the cancel call itself.

refundPercent.description: The policy band that applied, as a whole percentage: `100` (cancelled at or before the club's full-refund deadline), `50` (at or before the half-refund deadline), or `0` (later than that). Always `0` for a booking paid at the club (#354) — nothing was taken online, so nothing is due.

refundAmountCents.description: The refund due, in integer CENTS of the booking's currency. 50% of an odd total is ROUNDED, not floored. This is a QUOTE: the booking is cancelled, but the Stripe refund is a separate operation — do not tell the user the money has been returned.

reason.description: Why that band applied, as a human-readable string built server-side, e.g. `26.0h before start (>= 24h)` or `3.2h before start (< 12h)`. NOT the `reason` the client sent in the request body, and not machine-parseable — display it or ignore it.

CancelQuoteEnvelope.title: CancelQuoteEnvelope
CancelQuoteEnvelope.description: The success envelope wrapping the cancellation quote: `{"data": CancelQuote}`.

CheckoutRequest.title: CheckoutRequest
CheckoutRequest.description: Optional checkout body. The whole body may be omitted, which means card-only.

useWallet.description: Spend the player's club credit before charging the card. ONLY the literal JSON `true` enables it — `"true"`, `1`, `false`, a missing field, a missing body and an unparseable body all mean card-only. This strictness is deliberate: spending someone's credit because a field was omitted would take a decision that is theirs. Credit is capped at the booking total and at the available balance, so it can never overspend.

CheckoutSession.title: CheckoutSession
CheckoutSession.description: Everything the client needs to finish paying — or to know that there is nothing left to pay. Branch on `confirmed` first.

walletAppliedCents.description: How much club credit was spent, in integer CENTS. `0` when `useWallet` was not `true` or the balance was empty. Already debited from the ledger by the time this response is returned. Show it alongside `cardDueCents` so the user sees why the card amount is less than the booking price.

cardDueCents.description: How much is still to be charged to a card, in integer CENTS. `walletAppliedCents + cardDueCents` equals the booking's `totalCents`. `0` means credit covered everything.

paymentIntentId.description: The Stripe PaymentIntent id, or `null` when `cardDueCents` is 0 (no zero-amount intent is created — Stripe rejects those). Also stored on the booking for reconciliation.

clientSecret.description: The PaymentIntent client secret for the PaymentSheet. `null` when `cardDueCents` is 0. Can also be `null` in the unlikely event Stripe returns an intent without one — treat a `null` secret with `confirmed: false` as a failure to present the sheet, not as success.

publishableKey.description: The Stripe publishable key, returned here so the app needs neither a second config endpoint nor a rebuild to follow a key rotation. `null` if the server has no key configured — with `confirmed: false` that means the PaymentSheet cannot be presented.

confirmed.description: `true` when `cardDueCents` is 0: credit covered the whole price and this call has ALREADY confirmed the booking inline (through the same path the Stripe webhook uses). **Do not present a PaymentSheet** — go to the success screen. `false` means a card charge is still outstanding; present the sheet, and treat the booking as confirmed only once Stripe reports success. This response by itself never means "card paid".

CheckoutSessionEnvelope.title: CheckoutSessionEnvelope
CheckoutSessionEnvelope.description: The success envelope wrapping the checkout result: `{"data": CheckoutSession}`.

rating.description: Whole stars, 1 to 5. A string such as "5" is refused, not coerced.

body.description: Optional text. Sanitised to plain text on the way in. Omitted, null or whitespace-only means a star-only review, which skips moderation.

Review.title: Review
Review.description: The author's own view of the review they just left. It carries no author id and no moderation scores: the scores are for the moderator judging the classifier, and handed to an author they are a gauge for tuning text until it slips through.

bookingId.description: The booking that proved the visit.

body.description: The text as stored, after sanitising. Null for a star-only review.

status.description: Known values: `PUBLISHED`, `PENDING_REVIEW`, `REJECTED`. An open string rather than a closed enum, for the same reason as `Booking.status`: a shipped binary must not fail to decode a value added later. Only `PUBLISHED` counts toward the venue's `avgRating` and `reviewCount`.

TenantMeResponse.description: Success envelope produced by `ok(data)`. The payload is always under `data`; there is no unwrapped form.

tokenStale.description: True only when the token LISTS this club with a tenant id or role the database disagrees with — a web session signed in before a promotion or demotion. The edge middleware still refuses, from a listed role, a mutation it lacks, so a stale listing can refuse something the database would allow; the remedy is signing in again. Not an error: the rest of this payload is authoritative. Always false for a native access token, which lists no clubs — the edge defers those to the database (#250).

name.description: Display name. Null when the account has never set one.

TenantMeTenant.description: The club the caller is a member of.

id.description: Opaque tenant id (cuid). Compare against nothing; it is returned so a client can key local state per club.

slug.description: The slug used in `/t/{slug}/…`. Echoes the request path.

TenantMeMembership.description: The caller's membership AT THIS CLUB, read from the database — never from token claims.

role.description: The role held at this club, and only this club. A user may hold a different role at every club they belong to.

status.description: Membership status. In practice only `ACTIVE` is ever returned: the query filters on it, and any other status produces a 404. The other values are the field's domain, present so the enum does not have to change if the filter is relaxed.

permissions.description: Dotted permission strings derived server-side from `role` at this club. Not an open set in practice, but treat unknown values as opaque strings rather than failing to decode: permissions are added over time. Known values today: admin.venue_manage, admin.staff_manage, admin.pricing_manage, admin.billing_manage, admin.owner_management, admin.tenant_lifecycle, bookings.create, bookings.cancel, bookings.refund, bookings.view_all, courts.manage, availability.manage, coaches.list, coaches.manage_own_calendar, coaches.book, openplay.host, openplay.join, openplay.moderate, players.view, players.credit_adjust, payments.refund, payments.view.

joinedAt.description: When the membership was accepted, falling back to when it was created. RFC 3339, UTC, with NO fractional seconds — decodable by Swift's default `.iso8601` strategy.

ConnectOnboardingStartResponse.description: Success envelope produced by `ok(data)`. The payload is always under `data`; there is no unwrapped form.

stripeAccountId.description: The club's Stripe Express connected account id. Stable across calls once created.

onboardingUrl.description: Stripe-hosted onboarding URL to send the club admin to. Single-use and short-lived — a fresh one is minted on every call, so it must not be cached, persisted or shared. Stripe returns the admin to `/t/{slug}/settings/payouts?onboarding=complete`, or to `?onboarding=refresh` if the link expired (which should trigger a new call to this endpoint).

payoutsEnabled.description: Whether Stripe has actually approved the club for payouts. NOT set by this call — it is echoed from the stored venue row and only ever flipped to true by Stripe's `account.updated` webhook. It is normally false in this response even on a successful onboarding start, and finishing Stripe's form does not change it. Never treat a 200 from this endpoint as "payouts are live".

created.description: True when this call created the Stripe connected account; false when it reused an existing one and only minted a new link.

RealtimeTokenEnvelope.description: The success envelope produced by `ok(data)`. The payload is under `data`; nothing is returned at the top level.

RealtimeToken.description: A Centrifugo connection credential and where to spend it.

token.description: HS256 JWT, three base64url segments. Its claims are exactly `sub`, `iat` and `exp` — no channel grants, no role, no tenant.

expiresInSeconds.description: Lifetime of `token` in SECONDS from issuance (currently 900). This is a duration, not a timestamp. Refresh before it elapses: a minted token cannot be revoked, so this value is the revocation window.

url.description: The public Centrifugo WebSocket URL, from `NEXT_PUBLIC_CENTRIFUGO_URL`. NULL when that variable is unset on the server — the token is still minted and the response is still 200, so a client must handle null rather than assume a URL is always present.

CentrifugoSubscribeRequest.description: What Centrifugo POSTs to the subscribe proxy. `user` is a claim from the BROKER, not from the browser: Centrifugo derived it from the JWT this server signed, and the shared header secret is what makes it trustworthy. Additional properties are permitted and ignored.

user.description: The connecting user's id (a cuid). Marked required because Centrifugo always sends it; at runtime a missing, empty or non-string value is not a 4xx — it is answered HTTP 200 with the `403 forbidden` deny body, since every channel this server issues is personal and none is subscribable anonymously.

channel.description: The channel being joined. Recognised shapes: `conv:<cuid>`, `notif:<cuid>`, `presence:user:<cuid>`. Marked required because Centrifugo always sends it; a missing or unrecognised value is answered HTTP 200 with the `403 forbidden` deny body.

CentrifugoSubscribeResponse.description: Centrifugo's proxy decision. Exactly one of `result` or `error` is present; both arrive with HTTP status 200.

result.description: Always the empty object. This server attaches no subscription options (no info, data or expire_at).

CentrifugoSubscribeDeny.description: Subscription refused. The reason is logged server-side and never disclosed here — every refusal is byte-identical, so the response cannot be used to probe whether a conversation exists.

code.description: An INTEGER, unlike the string `code` used in this API's own error envelope. 403 for every refusal decision; 503 when `CENTRIFUGO_PROXY_SECRET` is unset on the server, in which case every request is refused.
Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, never on `message`.

message.description: Human-readable. Wording may change without notice.

requestId.description: Correlates with the server’s logs. Present on errors produced by the route wrapper, and on the inline errors from the platform routes; ABSENT on a few written inline by other handlers (the 401 from /auth/token, the 400 and 401 from /auth/refresh). Treat it as optional.

details.description: Present on some errors: validation issues, and the structured facts of a few domain refusals such as `BOOKING_LIMIT_REACHED` (`limit`, `upcoming`). Each operation documents its own.

bundleId.description: The app's bundle identifier. A token is only valid for the topic it was issued to.

environment.description: SANDBOX for debug builds, PRODUCTION for TestFlight and the App Store. REQUIRED and not defaulted: a missing value used to resolve to PRODUCTION, so a debug build's SANDBOX token was stored as PRODUCTION, sent to api.push.apple.com, rejected with BadDeviceToken and DELETED as a dead device — then re-registered on next launch and deleted again. The route now answers 400 rather than guessing.

PlatformCapability.description: What a platform grant permits. `TENANT_SUSPEND` is a WRITE capability, declared so the shape is settled and deliberately refused at runtime: taking a club offline is a power nobody has decided to ship. `REVIEW_MODERATE` is the one write that IS enabled, by owner decision: reading the review moderation queue and approving or rejecting its cases. Its reach is a review's visibility and the venue rating computed from it, nothing is deleted, and every decision is audited with the moderator's note. Since #262 every write capability — `REVIEW_MODERATE` included, for reading the queue as well as deciding — also needs a second-factor step-up on the calling session from the last 15 minutes (`POST /me/mfa/step-up`). `CONTACT_READ` (#369) reads the landing page's club enquiries: a read, no step-up. `CLUB_FEE_MANAGE` (#372) sets a club's fee terms: a write, behind a step-up.

actorUserId.description: The person. Written by `runAsPlatformAdmin`; a database trigger refuses any row whose value does not match `app.platform_admin_id` on the transaction, so it cannot be forged or written on somebody else’s behalf.

subjectTenantId.description: The club this was about, or null when it was about every club.

reason.description: Stated by the caller, at least 12 characters, never editable afterwards.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. NOT NULL in the schema, defaulting to 'BG'.

nextCursor.description: Null on the last page. Keep following it: a partially-read audit log that looks complete is the failure this endpoint exists to prevent.

phone.description: At least one of `phone` and `email` is set.

locale.description: The language the form was read in.

PlatformModerationCase.title: PlatformModerationCase
PlatformModerationCase.description: One open case about a review. No author: whether a review is abuse does not depend on who wrote it, and showing a name invites the idea that it should.

caseId.description: Pass to `/resolve`. Also the cursor value.

reason.description: Why it is queued: a classifier category, `classifier_unavailable`, or `user_report`. An open string.

scores.description: Classifier score per category, 0–1. Empty when no classifier ran.

status.description: `PENDING_REVIEW` for a held review, `PUBLISHED` for a reported live one, `REJECTED` for an automatic rejection awaiting a human. An open string.

note.description: Why. Stored as the case's resolution note and written verbatim to the platform audit row as its reason. No default.

review.description: Null only if the reviewed row no longer exists.

venue.description: The venue's rating after the decision. Null with `review`.

AccountKind.title: AccountKind
AccountKind.description: What the account IS (#263): `PLAYER`, `CLUB` (it runs exactly one club) or `COACH`. One account, one kind — doing two of these takes two accounts, and nothing switches between them. `null` is UNDECIDED: an account that held club roles at several clubs, or a coach role, when kinds arrived, and that the migration would not decide by rule. Typed as an open string for the same reason as `Booking.status`: treat an unrecognised value as undecided rather than failing the decode.

LandingReason.title: LandingReason
LandingReason.description:
Why the account lands where it does, for the client to map to a screen of its own. The server's web path is deliberately NOT sent.

- `player` — a PLAYER account: the player UI.
- `club` — a CLUB account whose club is live: that club's admin UI. `landing.club` names it.
- `club-unavailable` — a CLUB account whose one club is suspended or closed, or whose membership there ended. `landing.club` is null. Not the player UI: a club account is not a player.
- `coach` — a COACH account. There is no coach UI yet, on the web or anywhere, so today the web lands it on the player UI and `landing.club` is null.
- `undecided` — `accountKind` is null. Lands on its highest-ranked live club (OWNER over MANAGER over STAFF, then the oldest), named in `landing.club`; with none, the player UI and `landing.club` null.

An open string: treat an unrecognised value as `player`.

MeLandingClub.title: MeLandingClub
MeLandingClub.description: The club the account lands on, and the role it holds there.

role.description: The role held at that club: `OWNER`, `MANAGER` or `STAFF` (or `COACH`, once a coach home exists). An open string.

Me.title: Me
Me.description: The signed-in account, from the database — never from token claims.

name.description: Display name. Null when the account never gave one.

avatarUrl.description: The sign-in provider's picture (Google, Facebook), or null. Not writable: it comes with the sign-in.

sports.description: The sports this person plays, each at the level they declared (#359). In a stable order (the sport enum's); empty until they pick some. Set with `PATCH /me`.

club.description: Set when `reason` is `club`, or `undecided` with a live club; null otherwise.

MyBooking.title: MyBooking
MyBooking.description: One of the caller's own bookings, at any club: every field of `Booking`, plus the club it belongs to and where the caller stands on reviewing its venue. Produced by `toMyBookingDto` in `src/app/api/v1/_lib/dto.ts` — the same mapper the web page's server render is to use, so the two cannot drift. Flat rather than `allOf: [Booking, …]`, for the reason NOTES.md gives for `VenueDetail`. Since #358 the list also holds bookings the caller was ADDED to (`viewerRole: PARTICIPANT`).

id.description: Booking id. Also the value used as a pagination cursor.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Known values: `PENDING`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED`, `NO_SHOW`. Deliberately typed as an open string rather than a closed enum — a shipped iOS binary decoding a closed enum would fail outright on a status added later, and this codebase cannot hotfix a binary for a week. Treat an unrecognised value as "unknown" rather than failing the decode.

startTs.description: Start instant, RFC 3339 in UTC with NO fractional seconds (e.g. `2026-09-24T09:00:00Z`). Swift's default `.iso8601` strategy REJECTS fractional seconds, which is why the server strips them.

endTs.description: End instant, RFC 3339 UTC with no fractional seconds.

totalCents.description: The full booking price in integer CENTS of `currency`. Never a float, never a string. Computed server-side at creation and written down; it does not change afterwards.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for `totalCents`, e.g. `EUR` (the column default). Upper-case.

expiresAt.description: When a PENDING booking stops holding its slot — 15 minutes after creation. `null` once the booking is no longer merely held (confirmed, cancelled). A client should count down against this and stop offering payment when it passes.

cancelledAt.description: When the booking was cancelled, or `null` if it was not.

createdAt.description: When the booking was created. RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds.

cancellableUntil.description: The last instant the PLAYER may cancel this booking in the app (#354): the venue's cancellation cutoff (default 24 h, set by the club) before `startTs`, measured in elapsed hours. `null` when the booking is not cancellable at all (CANCELLED, COMPLETED, NO_SHOW). It may already be in the past: then only the club can cancel, and `POST …/cancel` answers 403 `CANCELLATION_CUTOFF_PASSED`. Render it in `venue.timezone`. RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds. Always `null` for a `PARTICIPANT`: only the booker cancels (#358).

resource.description: The court/pitch/table booked. Trimmed deliberately: no price, no status, no tenant id.

id.description: Resource id — the same value passed as `resourceId` when creating a booking.

resourceType.description: `ResourceType` (P51): COURT, FIELD, TABLE, BOARD_TABLE, LOBBY, ROUTE or TRACK. A TRACK (karting) is called a "писта" / "track", anything else a court. An open string, as `sport` here: show an unknown value as a court.

venue.description: The club/venue, lifted out of the resource so the wire shape survives a schema change that moves the relation.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. `Europe/Sofia`. The client needs it to render `startTs` as local wall-clock time rather than doing UTC arithmetic.

clubSlug.description: The club's slug — what `POST /t/{slug}/bookings/{id}/cancel`, `/checkout` and `/review` take for this booking. Null only if the club row is gone; such a booking can be shown and not acted on.

bookingId.description: The booking it was left against — at most one review per venue, so it may be ANOTHER of the caller's bookings there.

venueReview.description: The caller's own review of this booking's VENUE, or null if they have not written one.

canReview.description: Whether `POST /t/{clubSlug}/bookings/{id}/review` would be accepted now: the booking is COMPLETED and the venue has no review from the caller yet. Decided by the server so no client restates the rule.

viewerRole.description: The caller's side of the booking (#358): `BOOKER` made it; `PARTICIPANT` was added by the booker or an invite link. items.description: The caller's bookings at every club, newest `startTs` first. May be empty.

nextCursor.description: OPAQUE. Pass back verbatim as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page; never parse it. `null` means this is the last page. (It is currently the last item's `id`, but that is an implementation detail a client must not rely on.)

MyBookingPageEnvelope.title: MyBookingPageEnvelope
MyBookingPageEnvelope.description: `{"data":{"items":[...],"nextCursor":...}}` — doubly nested, like every v1 page.

eligible.description: May enrol: holds a live platform grant.

stepUpExpiresAt.description: When THIS session’s step-up stops counting; null if it has none.

qr.description: `otpauthUri` as a QR code (error correction M), drawn on the server so the secret never reaches a QR library in a browser or a third-party service. Draw it as `<svg viewBox="0 0 {size} {size}">` with a light background and `path` filled dark; the quiet zone (4 modules) is inside `size`. It encodes the secret: treat it like `otpauthUri`. A phone app enrolling itself has no use for it and can ignore it.

size.description: Side of the square in modules, quiet zone included: the SVG viewBox.

path.description: SVG path data (`d`) of every dark module, in module units.

recoveryCode.description: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX; case, spaces and hyphens are ignored.

SlotDuration.description: One length a free slot can be booked for (Q16), priced by the same quote `POST /t/{slug}/bookings` charges with, so the price shown is the price booked.

minutes.description: A whole number of `minBookingMinutes` units, at most `maxBookingMinutes`.

endTs.description: RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds: the slot start plus `minutes`. Send it as `endTs` when booking.

priceCents.description: Integer CENTS for the whole span, in the resource's `currency`.

MyBookingDetail.title: MyBookingDetail
MyBookingDetail.description: One of the caller's own bookings in full (#359): every field of `MyBooking`, with the venue block widened to what getting there needs, how it is paid, and who is playing. Produced by `toMyBookingDetailDto` in `src/app/api/v1/_lib/dto.ts`, the mapper the web's booking detail page renders through. Flat, like `MyBooking`.

id.description: Booking id. Also the value used as a pagination cursor.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Known values: `PENDING`, `CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED`, `NO_SHOW`. Deliberately typed as an open string rather than a closed enum — a shipped iOS binary decoding a closed enum would fail outright on a status added later, and this codebase cannot hotfix a binary for a week. Treat an unrecognised value as "unknown" rather than failing the decode.

startTs.description: Start instant, RFC 3339 in UTC with NO fractional seconds (e.g. `2026-09-24T09:00:00Z`). Swift's default `.iso8601` strategy REJECTS fractional seconds, which is why the server strips them.

endTs.description: End instant, RFC 3339 UTC with no fractional seconds.

totalCents.description: The full booking price in integer CENTS of `currency`. Never a float, never a string. Computed server-side at creation and written down; it does not change afterwards.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for `totalCents`, e.g. `EUR` (the column default). Upper-case.

expiresAt.description: When a PENDING booking stops holding its slot — 15 minutes after creation. `null` once the booking is no longer merely held (confirmed, cancelled). A client should count down against this and stop offering payment when it passes.

cancelledAt.description: When the booking was cancelled, or `null` if it was not.

createdAt.description: When the booking was created. RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds.

cancellableUntil.description: The last instant the PLAYER may cancel this booking in the app (#354): the venue's cancellation cutoff (default 24 h, set by the club) before `startTs`, measured in elapsed hours. `null` when the booking is not cancellable at all (CANCELLED, COMPLETED, NO_SHOW). It may already be in the past: then only the club can cancel, and `POST …/cancel` answers 403 `CANCELLATION_CUTOFF_PASSED`. Render it in `venue.timezone`. RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds. Always `null` for a `PARTICIPANT`: only the booker cancels (#358).

ProfileSport.title: ProfileSport
ProfileSport.description: A sport a player can declare (#359): the bookable sports of the registry that take a self-declared level. KARTING is bookable and is NOT one: playerz neither ranks nor matches drivers, so a level would seed nothing (P51), and `PATCH /me` refuses it with a 400. On the RESPONSE side treat it as an open string, as `Booking.status`: a sport added later must not fail a shipped decoder. On the request side only these values are accepted.

SportLevel.title: SportLevel
SportLevel.description: A sport the player plays, at the level they declared: 1 ("just starting") to 7 ("competitor"), Q37. Self-declared, not a rating; rankings (#378) take over from it.

UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest
UpdateMeRequest.description: At least one of the two. An absent field is left as it is. ANY other property is a 400 naming it (`details.field`), never ignored: this body writes the account row, which also holds the email, the kind and the language.

name.description: The display name other players see. Trimmed and inner runs of spaces collapsed before the length is checked. Letters in any script, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and dots; at least one letter. Cannot be cleared.

sports.description: The WHOLE list, replacing what is stored: a sport left out is removed, `[]` clears it. Each sport at most once.

DeskCustomer.description: Who a desk booking is for. The name and phone are what the desk took; the phone is normalised to E.164 (`0888 123 456` → `+359888123456`, `00…` → `+…`) and anything that is not a phone number is a 400. `userId` links one of the CLUB'S players (find one with `GET /t/{slug}/admin/customers`); the booking then appears in that player's own bookings. Another club's player and an unknown id are the same 404 `PLAYER_NOT_FOUND`.

SeriesRepeat.description: Every week, for `weeks` weeks, or until `until` inclusive. Exactly one of the two; at most 52 weeks (400 `INVALID_SERIES` past that, or for an `until` before `date`).

startTime.description: The club-local start, `HH:mm`, 24-hour. Resolved in the venue's timezone for each date, so a weekly series keeps its wall-clock time across a DST change.

priceCents.description: Staff's price in cents. Absent or null: the server's quote. An override is audited (`DESK_PRICE_OVERRIDDEN`, with the quote).

notes.description: The club's own note. Never shown to the linked player.

priceCents.description: Staff's price for EVERY week, in cents. Absent or null: each week's own quote.

notes.description: The club's own note. Never shown to the linked player.

skipDates.description: Weeks to leave out — the clashes the preview showed. A date that is not one of the series' weeks is ignored. Skipping every week is 400 `INVALID_SERIES`.

notes.description: The club's own note. Never shown to the linked player.

applyToSeries.description: For an occurrence of a series: also change every LATER live occurrence, and the series itself. Ignored for a booking with no series.

fromDate.description: The first club-local day to cancel. Every PENDING or CONFIRMED occurrence starting on or after it is cancelled.

status.description: `free`, `taken` (another booking holds the court) or `unavailable` (the club is closed then, the span is off its booking grid, or the time does not exist that day because the clocks skip it). Open string.

DeskPreviewEnvelope.description: The success envelope for a desk preview.

DeskCustomerMatch.description: One of the club's players. Never their phone number.

DeskCustomerMatchListEnvelope.title: DeskCustomerMatchListEnvelope
DeskCustomerMatchListEnvelope.description: The success envelope for a customer lookup.

status.description: Open string, as `Booking.status`. A desk booking is CONFIRMED when made.

deleted.description: The linked player deleted their account (#370): `name` is null and `email` empty; show "Deleted user".

remaining.description: Live occurrences from this one on, this one included.

series.description: The weekly series this booking is one week of, or null.

DeskBookingEnvelope.description: The success envelope for a desk booking.

bookingId.description: An ordinary booking: cancel one week with `POST /t/{slug}/bookings/{id}/cancel`.

priceCents.description: Staff's price for every week, or null for each week's quote.

occurrences.description: Every week that was booked, oldest first, cancelled ones included. Skipped weeks were never booked and are absent.

BookingSeriesEnvelope.description: The success envelope for a weekly series.

BookingPlayer.description: A person on a booking (#358). Display name and avatar ONLY: no user id, email or phone, for anybody, including to the other players.

participantId.description: What the booker removes this player by (`DELETE /me/bookings/{id}/participants/{participantId}`). Null for the booker, who is not removable. Not a user id.

name.description: Display name. Null for a registered player who has not set one.

avatarUrl.description: The sign-in provider's picture, or null.

isBooker.description: The person who made the booking (position 1).

registered.description: Has an account. False for a guest the booker named.

deleted.description: The player deleted their account (#370). The place stays, with `name` and `avatarUrl` null; show "Deleted user".

viewerRole.description: The caller's side of the booking (#358): `BOOKER` made it; `PARTICIPANT` was added by the booker or an invite link. A participant cannot cancel it (`cancellableUntil` is null for them) and leaves with `DELETE /me/bookings/{id}/participation`. A closed enum: the two sides of a booking are the model, not a status that grows.

capacity.description: The court's capacity: the booker plus up to `capacity - 1` added players.

spotsLeft.description: Places left for added players; 0 when full.

playersOpen.description: Whether players can be added, leave or be removed now: the booking holds its court (PENDING or CONFIRMED) and has not started.

liveInviteLinks.description: How many invite links are live (unrevoked, before the start). For the booker; null for a participant, who cannot see links.

userId.description: A `CoPlayer.userId` from `GET /me/bookings/{id}/co-players`. Any other id is 404.
What `POST /me/bookings/{id}/participants` takes. Only ever somebody the caller has played with.

token.description: 32 random bytes, base64url (43 characters). Returned HERE ONLY: the server keeps an HMAC of it and nothing else, never logs it and never audits it, so it cannot be shown again. Treat it as a secret until shared.

url.description: The page to share: `{site}/invite/booking/{token}`. Hand this to the share sheet.

expiresAt.description: The booking's start: the link stops working then. RFC 3339 UTC, no fractional seconds.

revoked.description: How many links this call stopped; 0 is not an error.

token.description: The token from the link (`/invite/booking/{token}`). In the BODY, never the path: a path is written to the request log, the trace and the metrics label.

BookingInvitePreview.title: BookingInvitePreview
BookingInvitePreview.description: What a link is for, before signing in. Nothing private: no surname, contact, price, other players or booking id.

timezone.description: IANA zone; render the times in it.

resourceType.description: `ResourceType` (P51): COURT, FIELD, TABLE, BOARD_TABLE, LOBBY, ROUTE or TRACK. A TRACK (karting) is called a "писта" / "track", anything else a court. An open string, as `sport` here: show an unknown value as a court.

bookerFirstName.description: The first word of the booker's display name; null when they have none.

joined.description: False when the caller was already on it (the booker included): a second tap is harmless.

kind.description: CLUB is never chosen: the owner creates club accounts.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: One bell row. Copy is already in the recipient's language.

VenuePhoto.title: VenuePhoto
VenuePhoto.description: One photo a club uploaded for a venue (#366): its cover or a picture of its gallery. Uploaded in the club admin, decoded and re-encoded on the server (EXIF and GPS stripped), and stored as WebP renditions. Every URL is ABSOLUTE and IMMUTABLE: a changed photo is a new URL, so a client may cache any of them indefinitely (the objects carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`). Pick from `variants` by the width you draw at (`srcset`-style); `url` is the default.

alt.description: The club's description of the photo, for screen readers (VoiceOver). Plain text, 1–200 characters, usually Bulgarian; never empty for a photo uploaded since #366, `""` only for an older row.

url.description: The default variant: 1280 px wide, or the widest below that.

width.description: Width of the LARGEST variant in pixels, for the aspect ratio. Null only for a row from before #366.

height.description: Height of the largest variant in pixels. Null only for a row from before #366.

variants.description: Every rendition, ascending by width: 640, 1280 and 1920 px, never wider than the upload (a 1000 px upload has 640 and 1000). WebP. Empty only for a row from before #366, which has just `url`.

blurDataUrl.description: A ~16 px wide WebP as a `data:image/webp;base64,…` URL: a placeholder to draw (scaled up, blurred) while the image loads.

StatementTotals.description: Sums of the lines. Reversals count negative.

revenueCents.description: The court price summed over the lines, integer cents.

feeCents.description: The fee due: the lines' rounded fees summed, integer cents.

kind.description: `CHARGE`: the booking was played. `REVERSAL`: a charge undone (a no-show marked after completion); its amounts are negative.

venueName.description: As it was when the line was written.

courtName.description: As it was when the line was written.

priceCents.description: The court price on the booking. Negative on a reversal.

feePercent.description: The rate the line was charged at, `"12.50"`.

freePeriod.description: Played inside the free period; the fee is 0.

feeCents.description: Rounded half-up to the cent. Negative on a reversal.

periodStart.description: The month's first instant at the club.

feePercent.description: The club's rate today. Each line carries its own.

feeStartsOn.description: The first day the fee is charged, at the club. Bookings before it are in the free period.

freePeriod.description: How much of the month the free period covers, on the club's terms today.

lines.description: By booking start. At most 10 000; the totals are always whole.

courtNouns.description: What the court column is called (P51): `track` at a club whose resources are all karting tracks ("Писта"), `mixed` at one with courts and tracks ("Корт / писта"), else `court` ("Корт"). Treat an unknown value as `court`.

feePercent.description: The percentage with two decimals, as a string: `"12.50"`.

feeStartsOn.description: The first day the fee is charged, at the club. Bookings before it are in the free period.

freePeriod.description: How much of the month the free period covers, on the club's terms today.

feePercent.description: 0–30 with at most two decimals. A string (`"12.5"`) is preferred: it never passes through a float.

feeStartsOn.description: The first day the fee is charged, at the club. Bookings before it are in the free period.

feeBps.description: The rate in basis points: 12.50% is 1250.

feePercent.description: The percentage with two decimals, as a string: `"12.50"`.

feeStartsOn.description: The first day the fee is charged, at the club. Bookings before it are in the free period.

share.description: online / (online + desk); null when there were no bookings.

startedAt.description: When the club was created on playerz.

active.description: A booking made in the last 14 days.

lastBookingAt.description: The newest qualifying booking's creation time within the 14-day window, or null.

trend.description: This month's share against last month's (±0.5 percentage points is flat); null when either month had no bookings.

weeks.description: The last 8 ISO weeks, oldest first.

venueName.description: Null when the venue has since been deleted.

timeZone.description: Always `Europe/Sofia`: every bucket is told in it.

PersonalDataExport.title: PersonalDataExport
PersonalDataExport.description: The personal-data export (#370). Additive: a later version may add sections and fields, never remove one without bumping `version`.

profile.description: The account: id, name, email, phone, picture, language, kind, when it was made, the sports with their levels, and the player profile if there is one.

providerAccounts.description: Always empty: an account is found by its email at every sign-in, and no provider id or token is stored.

addedPlayers.description: How many were added to it besides the booker; never who.
